record.original_question: Can one construct a Khovanov complex for arbitrary virtual knot diagrams, further develop the orientable-atom-based Khovanov homology for large classes of virtual links, and resolve the associated structural questions about K-full and Kho-full knots, optimal diagrams, minimality of classical crossings in virtual diagrams of classical knots, diagram moves preserving optimality, and the possibility of torsion in the B-state of virtual Khovanov homology?

evidence.quote: Construct a generalization of the Khovanov complex for the case of virtual knots that will work for arbitrary virtual diagrams. Investigate the Khovanov homology constructed in [91, 78].
Classify all K-full (Kho-full) knots. Are optimal diagrams always minimal with respect to the number of classical crossings? Classify all diagram moves that preserve optimality.

Is it true that if a classical knot K has minimal classical diagram with n crossings then any virtual diagram of K has at least n classical crossings? Can any virtual knot have torsion in the B-state of the Khovanov homology (the genuine leading term of some diagram)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following collection of structural problems concerning Khovanov-type homology theories for virtual knots and links.

Background. A virtual link diagram is a 4-valent plane graph whose vertices are decorated either as classical crossings (with over/under information) or as virtual crossings (encircled), considered up to generalized Reidemeister moves. Classical knots embed faithfully into virtual knots. For classical link diagrams, Khovanov's chain complex assigns to each crossing a 2-term resolution complex and produces a bigraded chain complex over Z whose homotopy type is a link invariant. An "atom" is a pair (M,Γ) consisting of a closed surface M and an embedded graph Γ with a checkerboard 2-coloring of M\Γ; an atom is orientable when its surface is. To a virtual diagram one associates an atom; if this atom is orientable, an integral Khovanov-type complex (the "orientable atom" Khovanov homology) can be built.

For a virtual knot K, let Kh(K) denote its (orientable-atom) Khovanov homology when defined. The B-state of the Khovanov complex denotes the homological summand coming from the all-B smoothing (i.e., the "genuine leading term" of the chain complex of a chosen diagram). A virtual knot diagram is called optimal if it realizes some agreed minimality of complexity for its equivalence class. A knot K is called K-full (respectively Kho-full) if its Kauffman bracket (respectively Khovanov homology) detects every feature of its diagrammatic complexity (in particular, the spread of its homology equals the number of crossings of a minimal diagram).

Problems.
(a) Construct a Khovanov chain complex over Z that is defined for arbitrary virtual link diagrams (not only those with orientable atom) and is invariant under generalized Reidemeister moves.
(b) Extend the orientable-atom Khovanov homology to as large a class of virtual links as possible and study its structural properties.
(c) Classify all K-full knots and all Kho-full knots.
(d) Is every optimal virtual diagram of a virtual knot minimal with respect to the number of classical crossings? Classify all local diagrammatic moves that preserve optimality.
(e) Prove or disprove: if a classical knot K has a minimal classical diagram with n crossings, then every virtual diagram of K has at least n classical crossings.
(f) Decide whether there exists a virtual knot whose B-state summand of the virtual Khovanov homology contains nontrivial torsion.
artifact.status_search_result: Part (a) has been substantially advanced: Manturov defined an integral Khovanov complex for arbitrary virtual link diagrams (with Z/2 coefficients trivially, and over Z via a doubling/orientable-atom construction), and Dye–Kaestner–Kauffman (arXiv:1409.5088) gave a Khovanov/Lee homology and Rasmussen invariant for virtual knots. Substantial parts of (b) have therefore been developed. The classification problems (c)–(d), the lower bound (e) on classical crossings in virtual diagrams of classical knots, and the torsion question (f) for the B-state appear in standard virtual-knot open-problem lists and have not been resolved in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Khovanov homology for virtual knots with arbitrary coefficients (Manturov)
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of an integral Khovanov-type homology for virtual knots with arbitrary diagrams, along the lines of Manturov.
status_evidence.claim: Problem (a) is partially solved via Manturov's construction of Khovanov homology for arbitrary virtual diagrams.

status_evidence.title: Khovanov Homology, Lee Homology and a Rasmussen Invariant for Virtual Knots (Dye–Kaestner–Kauffman)
status_evidence.snippet: Develops Khovanov and Lee homology and a Rasmussen invariant for virtual knots.
status_evidence.claim: Further development of Khovanov-type homology theories for virtual links has been carried out.

status_evidence.title: Virtual Knot Theory – Unsolved Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems including classification of K-full and Kho-full knots, optimality of diagrams, minimality of classical crossings in virtual diagrams of classical knots, and torsion in the B-state of virtual Khovanov homology.
status_evidence.claim: Problems (c)–(f) remain on standard open-problem lists in virtual knot theory.
